messages:
maria: uploaded an nsys capture for the warmup regression, timeline looks like repeated transfers serializing kernels. trace here: https://artifacts.internal/nsys/1997012345.nsys
kevin: taking a quick look — i can already see a pattern: HtoD blocks on the copy engine while kernels on other streams sit idle. could be pageable host fallbacks or copy-engine contention.
rishi: we use a small staging pool for host buffers. on pool miss we fall back to raw malloc and pass that ptr through. that might be causing unpinned fallback copies.
maria: here's the exact command i used to capture:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt,osrt_cupti -o /tmp/warmup.nsys \ 
  --capture-range=cpu:start,stop --sample=none --force-overwrite
```
kevin: nice. timeline snippet shows ~10ms HtoD spans labeled "cudaMemcpy" interleaved with 2-3ms kernels. copy engine (stream 2) does back-to-back copies: they look serialized. cpu lanes show 20-30ms gaps on worker threads aligning with those copies. could be scheduler preemption or our mutex around the staging pool.
julia: quick question — are those host buffers registered/pinned? if not, driver will do implicit pin+copy which is synchronous and expensive. also ensure we call cudaMemcpyAsync on non-default streams.
perf-bot: auto-insight: memcpy size distribution peaked at ~4MB, transfer count per request ~6.
kevin: interesting. if transfers are medium-sized and frequent, small fragmentation + unpinned fallbacks double the overhead. batching heuristics may be causing prefetches to fire per item instead of coalescing.
rishi: current prefetch policy: for batch_size < 8 we prefetch per item; for >=8 we aggregate into a single prefetch call. this was tuned for latency, but maybe it's hurting throughput.
maria: hypothesis: pool misses -> fallback malloc -> unpinned ptrs -> driver-stage copies -> copy-engine serialization -> kernels blocked -> observed CPU gaps (waiting on io or lock).
kevin: to test: (A) force pool to use cudaHostAlloc (pinned) for staging, (B) run same workload, (C) capture nsys and perfetto to correlate CPU-sched events. also try toggling stream assignments: put memcpys on a dedicated copy stream with cudaMemcpyAsync + proper stream tagging.
julia: i'll flip the pool to pinned on dev4 and run the repro. if hostcopy times shrink and cpu gaps disappear, that points to unpinned fallbacks. if not, try disabling prefetch aggregation and see if coalescing helps.
maria: added a small repro script in the artifact bucket: s3://redwood-dev/perf/repro_warmup.tar.gz. it contains a minimal runner that mimics kvcache prefetch pattern.
kevin: other useful captures: nvprof to get api-level stacks, and a perfetto trace to see thread scheduling (SCHED_SWITCH). nsys hides some kernel->cpu scheduling alignment.
rishi: i'll run the 3 variants tonight: fallback malloc (baseline), pool pinned (test A), aggregated-prefetch-only (test B). post timelines back here.
maria: perfect. thanks all — if we confirm pinned pool fixes it we should also update the batching heuristic so prefetch aggregation happens earlier for busy tails. :thumbsup:
